items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory and may be arranged for through Port Adelaide. The pilot embarks about 2.5 miles E of the jetty in Port Giles. The port uses VHF radio channels 6,8,12,13,16 and 67 and the call sign “Port Giles VTS.” Flinders Ports VTS must be informed of any mechanical or navigational defect.

notes.quote: Additionally, AIS must be active 30 minutes before pilot boarding and throughout duration of that service.
Tug requirements by vessel LOA can be found through Port Adelaide on VHF 06.
Notice of arrival is required 24 hours in advance; the ETA should be confirmed 4 hours before arrival.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels. The pilot boards about 1 mile E of the berth in 34°27.4'S 137°56.8'E. The port uses VHF radio channels 6, 12 and 16 and the call sign Adelaide VTS.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is not compulsory, but pilots can be arranged through Port Adelaide (see paragraph 8.51).

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels should contact the port on VHF channel 16 to obtain berthing clearance.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for all vessels over 35m in length entering Outer Harbor or Port Adelaide Harbor, unless exempt. Pilots board SW of the Entrance Lighted Buoy in position 34°49.0'S, 138°20.0'E. Pilotage is available 24 hours, but vessels are not turned in the harbor at night. Pilots must be requested 2 hours in advance, or 4 hours in advance if outside of office hours, to the harbormaster.

notes.quote: Notice of arrival is required 24 hours in advance; the ETA should be confirmed 4 hours before arrival.
See Regulations for additional reporting requirements.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Flinders Ports VTS must be informed of any mechanical or navigational defect. Additionally, AIS must be active 30 minutes before pilot boarding and throughout duration of that service. A single tug is required for vessels turning or having an LOA of over 90m. Two tugs are required for vessels over 120m and three for vessels over 230m.

calls.quote: Vessels must report to Adelaide VTS on VHF channel 12 or 16, as follows: 1.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: A pilot boarding station is established in position 12°07.6S., 96°50.6'E, close ENE of the mooring buoys. Limited pilotage advice is available from the port administration which claims no responsibility for this information.

items.head: Directions
items.quote: It was reported (1986) that the least depth in the channel is 2.8m W of Beacon No. 5. The beacons have been reported to be unreliable. An alternative track, with a least depth of 4.1m, runs direct from Beacon No. 3 to Beacon No. 8. Vessels with drafts up to 4.1m, and on occasion 4.7m, have used the channel at HW.

items.head: Pilotage
items.quote: Pilotage is compulsory for vessels over 150 GT The pilot boards 1 mile W of Smith Point and the service is available in daylight hours. Vessels should not approach the moorings nearer than 1 mile until the pilot has embarked. There is a port radio station at Christmas Island. The vessel’s ETA should be sent 48 hours and 24 hours prior to arrival.

items.head: Regulations
items.quote: Vessels must not approach the moorings in Flying Fish Cove closer than 1 mile without instructions.
